w:r.w:t: React and Node.js store with a complete administration panel
Prepared 30 October 2026 | Product specification and engineering guide

Build a single store where you upload products and categories, sell to registered customers or guests, accept approved payment methods, track shipments, and manage the full order lifecycle. The design follows the search-first structure and deal cards in your eBay screenshots, with your own brand and visual identity.

Use Next.js for the React storefront and admin interface, Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui, a NestJS Node.js API, PostgreSQL, and background workers. Render product content on the server so visitors and search engines receive useful HTML. Keep inventory, orders and payments authoritative in PostgreSQL.
One merchant, fixed-price products, physical goods, category hierarchy and variants.
Accounts with sign in and sign out, plus guest checkout without registration.
Provider adapters; confirm merchant eligibility before integration. Payoneer Checkout is conditional.
Automatic SEO foundations, useful product content, measured acquisition and consent-based email.
Multi-seller onboarding, auctions, seller payouts and complex marketplace disputes require a separate release.
No strategy can guarantee rankings or 100% customer conversion. The goal is a reliable store and a measurable process that improves qualified traffic, purchase rate and repeat orders.
UI references, storefront, administration and architecture
Data schemas, SQL foundations, API controllers and project setup
Security, checkout, payments, shipping and automatic publishing
SEO, customer acquisition, privacy, email and development phases
Acceptance tests, operations, code patterns and source references

Use the browsing logic visible in the supplied screens: a prominent search bar, category navigation, a wide promotion area, and product cards with clear prices. Use original photography, copy, logo and colors for your own store.

Translate the references into your store

Place search ahead of decoration. Give each product an uncluttered image area, a two-line name, current price, genuine discount information, delivery estimate and wishlist action. Use one primary action per context. Promotional banners should link to real collections with valid stock and dates.
For a first visit, promote categories and deals. Show account benefits as a secondary invitation while keeping shopping and guest checkout available.
Utility bar, logo, category menu, search, account, cart, curated hero, category tiles, deals, best sellers and trust information.
Breadcrumbs, result count, query suggestions, filters, sort, product grid, crawlable pagination and useful empty states.
Gallery, title, brand, variant selectors, live price, availability, delivery estimate, returns, specifications, genuine reviews and related items.
Editable quantities; totals; coupon validation; guest or account choice; address; shipping; approved payments; final review.
Orders, shipment timeline, invoices, addresses, wishlist, returns, profile, marketing choices and session management.
Secure guest tracking, contact form, help articles, return policy, shipping policy, privacy notice and accessible support link.

Start with white surfaces, dark text, a single blue or green primary color, neutral borders, and restrained shadows. Suggested tokens: page background #FFFFFF; text #111827; primary #2563EB; muted #F3F4F6; border #D1D5DB. Use an 8 px spacing scale, 12 to 16 px card radii, and a consistent square product image ratio. Final colors must pass contrast checks.
Two product columns where readable; full-width search; filter drawer; sticky purchase action that does not obscure content.
Three product columns; compact navigation; responsive cart and checkout summaries.
Four to six columns depending on card width; left filters; centered container up to about 1440 px.

Use shadcn/ui navigation, sheet, dialog, tabs, select, form, skeleton, pagination and toast components. Build admin tables with TanStack Table. Choose one component primitive family and use it consistently. [8, 19, 20]

Include visible keyboard focus, semantic headings, labeled inputs, descriptive errors, meaningful image alt text and reduced motion. Aim for WCAG 2.2 AA. Prefer a static hero; if a carousel is added, provide pause and keyboard controls. Test checkout with keyboard and screen readers.
4 Administration panel that operates the business

Every admin action must persist through the API, enforce permissions and show clear progress, validation and recovery states. A dashboard is complete only when staff can perform the daily workflows below.
Revenue excluding failed payments; paid and COD orders separated; pending fulfillment; low stock; date ranges; drill-through reports.
Draft, preview, publish, schedule, archive, duplicate, variants, images, SKU, SEO overrides, bulk edit and CSV import with row errors.
Nested categories, sorting, attributes, landing content and redirects when URLs change; reject hierarchy cycles.
Stock receipt, adjustment with reason, reservation visibility, low-stock thresholds and append-only movement history.
Search, detail, notes, fraud hold, packing, partial shipment, cancellation, invoice and customer notifications.
Provider references, reconciliation, partial refund, return approval, inspection, restock decision and dispute evidence.
Order history, addresses, support context and consent status; authorized exports only; no password visibility.
Dated coupons, redemption limits, banners, collections, SEO validation, redirects, feeds and approved email segments.
Zones, rates, couriers, tracking, taxes, locale, payment configuration status and email templates.
Invitations, roles, MFA enrollment, session revocation and searchable action history.

Owner manages roles and integrations. Catalog staff edit products and stock. Fulfillment staff access orders and shipments. Support staff see only necessary customer details. Finance staff reconcile and refund. Marketing staff manage content and consented audiences. Check each permission on the server; hiding a button is only a UI convenience.

A catalog editor creates a product, adds images and variants, enters opening stock, validates the preview and publishes. Fulfillment staff receive a paid order, generate a packing list, create a shipment and record tracking. Finance can issue a partial refund with a reason. Every change records the actor and timestamp.

Start with a modular monolith: one API codebase with clear domain modules, plus a separate worker process. It is easier to operate than early microservices and preserves transaction boundaries for stock and orders.
Next.js App Router and TypeScript. Public catalog uses server rendering and explicit caching. Admin and account data are private and uncached.
Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui, Lucide icons, React Hook Form and Zod for client validation. Mirror critical rules in server DTOs.
TanStack Query for interactive server state; TanStack Table for admin grids; Recharts for simple charts. Keep cart totals server-authoritative.
NestJS with Express adapter, validation pipes, permission guards, domain services and OpenAPI documentation.
PostgreSQL with versioned migrations. Prisma is a suitable typed ORM; use parameterized SQL for locks and specialized indexes.
Redis and BullMQ for jobs; PostgreSQL transactional outbox for durable publication, email and reconciliation events.
S3-compatible object storage and CDN. Begin with PostgreSQL full-text search; add Meilisearch or OpenSearch after measured need.
Vitest or Jest, Playwright, structured logs, OpenTelemetry and an error tracker. Pin compatible supported package versions.

Browser requests go to the Next.js application and a same-origin /api/v1 reverse proxy to NestJS. NestJS reads and writes PostgreSQL. It calls payment and courier adapters only from the server. Workers consume durable outbox events and send email, refresh search documents, invalidate catalog caches and update product feeds.

The browser receives publishable provider configuration only. Database credentials, payment secrets, webhook secrets and signing keys stay in server secret storage. Separate development, staging and production databases, buckets and provider credentials.

Next.js remains a React application and supports your requested stack. Its server rendering and metadata APIs give product pages and category pages a stronger technical foundation than relying only on a browser-rendered SPA. NestJS owns commerce rules; Next.js owns page composition. [4, 5, 17, 18]
6 Database schema for identity and catalog

Use UUID primary keys, UTC timestamptz timestamps and explicit foreign keys. In the tables below, PK means primary key, FK means foreign key, UQ means unique, and ? means nullable. Field lists are the implementation dictionary, including the supporting entities required beyond the starter SQL.
id PK, email_normalized UQ, password_hash?, name, phone?, status, email_verified_at?, created_at
Never store plaintext passwords. Social-only accounts may omit password_hash.
sessions: id, user_id FK, token_hash UQ, expires_at, revoked_at?; auth_tokens: user_id, kind, token_hash, expires_at, used_at?
Rotate session IDs on login; consume reset and verification tokens once.
roles, permissions, user_roles, role_permissions; each join uses a composite PK
Permission keys such as products.publish and orders.refund.
id, user_id FK, recipient, phone, country, region, city, postal_code?, address lines
Address book is editable; order addresses are independent snapshots.
id PK, parent_id? FK to categories, slug UQ, name, description, sort_order, active
Prevent cycles in service; publish only useful category landing pages.
id, slug UQ, title, brand?, description, status, primary_category_id FK, published_at?, version
Status: draft, scheduled, published, archived. Explicit publish validation.
id, product_id FK, sku UQ, gtin?, option_values jsonb, price_minor, compare_at_minor?, currency, active
Each sellable item has a variant, including products with no visible options.
product_media: product_id, variant_id?, object_key, alt_text, sort_order; attributes, category_attributes, product_attribute_values
Validate file type and dimensions. Typed attributes power reliable filters.

A category has many products and may have child categories. A product has many variants and media assets. Add product_categories(product_id, category_id) with a composite PK when a product belongs to several collections; retain one primary category for breadcrumbs. A variant has stock records per warehouse.

Use product_seo(product_id PK/FK, meta_title?, meta_description?, canonical_override?, index_policy, content_version). Keep generated defaults separate from staff overrides so later imports do not erase editorial work.
7 Database schema for checkout and money
variant_id FK, warehouse_id FK, on_hand, reserved; composite PK
CHECK on_hand >= 0, reserved >= 0 and reserved <= on_hand.
id, order_id FK, variant_id FK, warehouse_id FK, quantity, expires_at, state
UQ order/variant/warehouse. States active, committed, released. Changes are atomic.
id, variant_id, warehouse_id, delta_on_hand, delta_reserved, reason, reference, actor_id?, created_at
Append-only history. Prevent duplicate movements for the same event and action.
cart: id, user_id?, guest_token_hash?, expires_at; item: cart_id, variant_id, quantity
UQ cart/variant; quantity > 0. Merge on login without exceeding stock.
id, order_number UQ, user_id?, email, phone, order_status, payment_status, fulfillment_status, currency, totals_minor, address snapshots
Guest orders have user_id NULL. Freeze prices, addresses, tax and delivery at placement.
id, order_id FK, variant_id?, sku_snapshot, title_snapshot, options_snapshot, quantity, unit_price_minor, discount_minor, tax_minor
Product edits or archive must never change historical order amounts.
id, order_id FK, provider, provider_reference UQ per provider, amount_minor, currency, state, idempotency_key
One order can have multiple attempts; only verified payment results change paid status.
refunds: payment_id, amount_minor, reason, state, provider_ref; returns: order_id, state; return_items: order_item_id, quantity, disposition
Lock against over-refunds; count completed and pending refunds. Restock after inspection.
shipments: order_id, carrier, tracking_number, state; shipment_items: shipment_id, order_item_id, quantity; tracking_events: shipment_id, event_key, occurred_at, status
Multiple shipments per order. UQ carrier event identity; enforce remaining quantities.

Store amounts as BIGINT minor units plus ISO currency, and serialize large amounts as decimal strings in JSON. Use currency exponent metadata; never assume every currency uses two decimals. Avoid JavaScript floating-point arithmetic for money. Keep authorized, captured, refunded and settled amounts distinct.

Order total equals line subtotals minus allocated discounts plus tax and shipping. Store provider fees, net settlement, currency conversion and settlement batches separately. Gross sales and available cash are different reports. Do not combine unlike currencies into one unconverted total.
8 Database schema for growth and operations
coupon: code UQ, type, value, currency?, min_spend, starts_at, ends_at, usage_limit; redemption: order_id FK, coupon_id FK, amount
Enforce limits transactionally; allocate discounts to items for partial refunds.
wishlist_items(user_id, product_id) composite PK; reviews(user_id, product_id, order_item_id?, rating, body, status)
Reviews require moderation; verified purchase label requires actual purchased item.
id, subject_id, purpose, action, source, policy_version, occurred_at
Append-only grant/withdrawal evidence. Maintain current effective consent separately.
contacts: email_normalized UQ, user_id?, marketing_state; email_jobs: campaign_id, contact_id, state, provider_message_id
Suppress unsubscribed, bounced or complained addresses before every marketing send.
event_id UQ, anonymous_id?, user_id?, name, properties, occurred_at, consent_version
Allowlisted properties; no email, card data, address or free-text search PII by default.
banners, collections, pages, product_seo, url_redirects(from_path UQ, to_path, status_code), feed_jobs
Editorial overrides and version history; reject redirect loops and external redirect abuse.
outbox_events: id, type, aggregate_id, aggregate_version, payload, processed_at?; webhook_events: provider, event_id UQ per provider, state
Persist before acknowledging a valid webhook; retries and duplicate delivery are normal.
audit_logs: actor_id, action, entity_id, redacted_diff, request_id, created_at; integrations: provider, secret_reference, enabled
No secret values in audit logs. Separate authority to configure integrations.
idempotency_keys: scope, actor_key, key, request_hash, response_ref, expires_at; guest_access_tokens: order_id, token_hash, expires_at
UQ scope/actor/key; a reused key with another payload returns conflict.

Index every high-volume FK and common query: orders(user_id, created_at), orders(email_normalized, created_at), products(status, published_at), variants(product_id), payments(order_id), and tracking_events(shipment_id, occurred_at). Use GIN for full-text search and measured JSONB filters; avoid indexing every attribute blindly.

Use a unique index on lower(email) or normalize before writing. Archive products rather than cascading deletion into orders. Redact or anonymize customer data through a controlled retention process while preserving legally required order records. Audit access and test backup restoration.
9 Starter SQL for catalog and inventory

This PostgreSQL foundation illustrates the field types and constraints. Extend it with the supporting tables on pages 6 to 8, version it through migrations and test it against an empty database before development branches depend on it. Application validation must supplement database checks.
active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true
primary_category_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES categories(id),
updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
product_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES products(id),
active BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true

Generate UUIDs in the application or use a supported database UUID function. Add created_at and updated_at consistently, and enforce updated_at in your write layer or a database trigger. Reserve product version numbers for optimistic concurrency and event ordering.
10 Starter SQL for orders and event safety
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
order_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(id),
received_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

Add separate state enums or CHECK constraints for each status axis, payment and refund tables, totals breakdown, reservations and shipment items before checkout is released. Add a partial index on unprocessed outbox rows and bounded retention for webhook payloads. Never store unredacted payment credentials in JSONB.

Use /api/v1 as the public API prefix and OpenAPI as the contract. Controllers accept DTOs, authenticate callers and delegate to services. Services own stock, pricing and state transitions; repositories own database access. Return only allowlisted response fields.
Public or session as appropriate; rate limits; generic recovery responses; CSRF on browser mutations.
Authenticated owner only. Reauthenticate sensitive changes and revoke sessions when required.
Public published products only; validated filters, bounded page size and deterministic sort.
Session-bound account cart or high-entropy guest cart cookie; no client price acceptance.
Guest or account; cart capability or ownership; idempotency on placement and payment creation.
Authenticated owner or narrowly scoped guest capability; state-based cancellation rules.
Generic request response, short-lived code or link, rate limit and order-scoped session.
Account owner; validate purchased item before verified-purchase label; moderation before display.
Separate purpose flags; verification and abuse limits; unsubscribe works without account login.

Use a request ID in every response. Validation errors identify fields without leaking internals. Typical outcomes: 201 created; 400 invalid input; 401 no valid session; 403 forbidden; 404 unavailable resource; 409 stock, version or idempotency conflict; 422 unsupported business action; 429 throttled. Use a consistent JSON shape: code, message, fieldErrors and requestId.

Never let a URL order ID alone grant access. Staff access, customer ownership and guest capabilities are independent authorization paths. Enforce query limits server-side and paginate expensive lists.
products.read/write/publish. Use If-Match or expectedVersion on updates; validate bulk operations.
categories.write; validate cycles, URL changes and product reassignment.
inventory.read/adjust; append movement, reason and actor; prohibit direct balance overwrite.
orders.read/manage and shipments.create; reject invalid transitions and excess quantities.
payments.refund; MFA step-up; maximum refundable amount; idempotent provider call.
customers.read/export; field-level masking and audited export purpose.
marketing.write/send; preview, test recipient, suppression check and campaign approval.
settings.write, staff.manage or audit.read; owner privileges are not granted through profile edits.
Provider signature verification over raw bytes, event deduplication, durable receipt and retries.
Service authentication and replay controls; never accept an arbitrary URL or job command.

Register a global validation pipe, session guard and permission guard. Mark public endpoints explicitly. Add audit interceptors to sensitive admin operations, an exception filter for safe error responses, and request-size limits before parsing. Webhooks bypass browser CSRF only because they use provider authentication; they do not bypass signature verification. [17, 18]

ProductService owns catalog writes; InventoryService owns movements and reservations; CheckoutService freezes totals; PaymentService coordinates adapters and reconciliation; OrderService enforces order actions; ShipmentService maps courier states. Controllers must not contain ad hoc SQL or duplicate payment logic.

Use a TypeScript monorepo with one package manager and a lockfile. Select a supported Node.js LTS at kickoff, pin compatible package versions, and document upgrade ownership. Keep API and UI contracts shared without importing server secrets into the frontend.
apps/web/ Next.js React storefront and admin
apps/worker/src/ Outbox, emails, feeds and retries
packages/contracts/ OpenAPI types and event schemas
APP_URL, API path, supported locale and storefront currency
Provider publishable key only when documented for browser use
Public image CDN base URL; no credentials in NEXT_PUBLIC variables

Create the monorepo; configure linting and type checks; run local PostgreSQL, Redis and object storage; apply migrations; seed categories and permissions; create the first owner through a one-time administrative command; enroll MFA; generate OpenAPI clients; add CI. Validate required environment variables on process startup and fail closed if secrets are missing.
Build a vertical slice first: publish one product, browse it, place one guest test order, verify payment, dispatch it and view tracking. Complete that path before expanding decorative screens.

Registration normalizes email, hashes the password with Argon2id, stores an unverified account and sends a single-use verification link. Login checks credentials, throttles attempts, rotates the session token and records a server-side session. Logout revokes that session and clears the cookie. Password reset expires existing sessions according to the recovery policy. [9]

Use a mature authentication library or carefully reviewed module. Allow password managers, long passphrases and breached-password checks. Provide generic login and recovery responses where appropriate to reduce account enumeration. Admin staff must enroll MFA, with audited recovery.
__Host-session with Secure, HttpOnly, Path=/, no Domain and SameSite=Lax for the same-origin architecture.
High-entropy random session token in cookie; store its hash server-side. Keep roles and revocation authority on the server.
Starting policy: customers 7 days idle and 30 days absolute; staff 30 minutes idle and 12 hours absolute. Tune after risk review.
Validate CSRF token and allowed Origin on browser state changes. SameSite alone is not the entire CSRF defense.
Reauthenticate for email change, MFA reset, role changes, gateway configuration and refunds. Notify the account owner.
Do not put bearer authentication tokens in localStorage. Cart UI state can be local; authoritative cart access is protected.

Checkout collects the delivery and contact details needed to fulfill the order and leaves orders.user_id empty. Do not create a password or subscribe the buyer silently. Email the receipt and a secure access path. Allow a later account invitation without blocking the purchase.

Guest tracking begins with order number and email, returns a generic result, then sends a one-time link or code. Store only a token hash, expire it quickly, and exchange it for a restricted order session. Redact addresses on tracking views and set Referrer-Policy: no-referrer on token exchange pages.

Claiming a guest order requires verification of the same email address. A matching typed email is insufficient. After verification, link only the relevant orders and record the action. Protect lookup, verification and resend endpoints with rate and abuse limits.
Deny by default; server-side permission and object ownership checks on every protected route.
A second customer cannot read or modify another customer order.
DTO allowlists, parameterized queries, rich-text sanitization, URL validation and bounded filters.
Invalid fields rejected; stored script content cannot execute.
Calculate totals server-side; verify signed callbacks and provider status; compare order, amount and currency.
Browser return URL cannot mark an unpaid order paid.
Row locks or conditional stock updates, database transactions, uniqueness and idempotent side effects.
Concurrent attempts to buy the last unit produce one successful allocation.
HTTPS, HSTS after validation, strict CSP, clickjacking protection, safe redirects and least-privilege CORS.
Approved payment SDK works; unapproved script origin is blocked.
Presigned upload, size/type limits, magic-byte check, image re-encoding, malware checks and private staging.
An executable or oversized file cannot become a public product image.
Secret manager, rotation, encryption at rest, log redaction and separate production credentials.
No password, full card, token or sensitive address appears in logs.
Rate limits, suspicious login alerts, checkout velocity checks and risk-based challenges.
Retry abuse is throttled without blocking normal guest purchase.
Dependency lockfile, security review, vulnerability scan and minimal runtime permissions.
Build uses reviewed artifacts and no known critical exploitable dependency.
Private database network, least-privilege service users, admin MFA and immutable audit export.
Restoration succeeds; privilege change and refund have traceable actors.

Use hosted checkout or provider-hosted fields. Keep PAN and CVV outside your application, logs and database; store only provider references and permitted masked metadata. This reduces card-data exposure but does not automatically remove all PCI obligations. Confirm the applicable validation scope with the payment provider.

Include IDOR tests, account recovery tests, expired session tests, CSRF rejection, webhook replay, duplicate refunds, malicious upload, unauthorized export and concurrent stock tests. Security acceptance belongs in each phase, with a focused review before accepting live payments. [9, 10]

Guest and registered buyers use the same pricing and inventory services. Treat the cart as a request to purchase; it does not reserve stock indefinitely. Present a final quote with an expiry and recalculate it when placing the order.
Accept variant IDs, quantities, address, shipping choice and coupon. Resolve the cart from its session or guest capability. Ignore client prices and totals.
Require an idempotency key scoped to the actor and operation. Persist a request hash; the same key and payload returns the same order, while a changed payload returns conflict.
In a database transaction, lock stock rows in deterministic order, validate available stock and allocate discounts, tax and shipping from current server rules.
Create the pending order and immutable line and address snapshots. Reserve stock for a defined payment window, for example 15 minutes where the provider supports it. Add outbox events and commit.

Outside the database transaction, create the provider checkout session with a stable payment attempt ID and provider idempotency where available. Persist the reference. Never hold stock-row locks while making a network call.

On a verified successful capture, lock the order, payment and reservations. Check reference, amount and currency. Commit stock once, update payment state and enqueue the confirmation through the outbox.
Two buyers want the final unit
Only one reservation succeeds; the other receives a clear stock conflict and a refreshed cart.
Cancel or expire the attempt, release its active reservation once and allow a controlled retry.
Query or reconcile the existing attempt before creating another charge; show processing rather than false failure.
Attempt atomic reallocation; if unavailable, place on exception hold and refund according to policy. Do not silently oversell.
Record payment_due and payment method COD. Allocate stock after confirmation; record collection and courier remittance separately.
Freeze accepted totals on the placed order. Requote before placement if the original quote is no longer valid.
Do not report a payment authorization as captured revenue. Support authorized, captured, failed, cancelled, partially refunded and refunded payment states independently from shipping. [10]

A Payoneer receiving account or balance is not automatically a retail checkout gateway. Payoneer Request a Payment is intended for business payments and is not a substitute for consumer ecommerce checkout. Payoneer Checkout is the relevant product, subject to merchant eligibility. [1, 2]

At review, Payoneer’s Checkout page states the service is provided exclusively to US and Hong Kong entities; its interest form also mentions a Hong Kong entity and monthly webstore volume above USD 20,000. Obtain written confirmation for your legal entity, business model and volume before making this the launch dependency. [1]
Implement only after approval and access to the documentation for the exact product offered. Supported cards and wallets vary by integration and market.
Evaluate Safepay as a local acquiring option for domestic and international payments. Confirm product eligibility, currencies, settlement bank, refunds and enabled methods. [3]
Enable only the methods present in your approved gateway contract. Confirm JazzCash, Easypaisa or other requested rails individually; a generic wallet logo is not proof of support.
Useful where your fulfillment and reconciliation process supports them. Transfers remain pending until independently verified; uploaded receipts alone cannot mark paid.
Optional later feature for non-withdrawable promotional credit with a ledger. Payoneer settlement is separate from a customer wallet.

Store the provider reference and present only returned, allowlisted checkout URLs. Verify callbacks using that provider’s current signing scheme over raw bytes. Persist authenticated events durably, acknowledge promptly, then process with retries. Never invent Payoneer endpoints or assume one provider’s webhook API matches another.

Collect business registration and KYC, settlement bank details, website policies, product restrictions, fees, FX terms, settlement timing, reserve policy and dispute process. In staging, test success, decline, cancellation, duplicate event, missing event, partial refund and reconciliation. No provider accepts every payment method in every country.
Separate order payment and fulfillment states

Order states: pending, confirmed, on_hold, cancelled and completed. Payment states: unpaid, processing, authorized, captured, partially_refunded, refunded and failed. Fulfillment states: unfulfilled, partially_shipped, shipped, delivered and returned. Derive customer labels from these axes rather than one overloaded status field.
Freeze order details, record payment state and send the correct receipt or pending-payment notice.
Order received with item list and payment result.
Payment verified or COD confirmation accepted; warehouse allocation and fraud hold reviewed.
Create carrier shipment, label and tracking reference; assign shipped quantities to order items.
Carrier, tracking link and shipped items.
Authenticate carrier webhook or poll the carrier API; normalize events and preserve raw status mapping.
Timeline with last update time and delivery estimate.
Record delivered, delayed, failed delivery or returned-to-origin. Alert staff about unresolved exceptions.
Delivered status or clear next step and support action.
Approve eligible items, receive goods, inspect, choose restock disposition and process refund.
Return progress and refund amount with expected processing information.

Choose a courier after checking coverage, COD remittance, tracking API access, labels, pickup workflow, claims and return-to-origin costs. Implement a carrier adapter with createShipment, cancelShipment and fetchTracking. Start with one carrier and allow a staff-entered tracking fallback with audit history.

Deduplicate carrier events, store their occurrence time and prevent a delayed in-transit message from overwriting delivered status. Support multiple packages, partial shipment and separate tracking numbers. Show the most recent successful synchronization; do not display “live” when the courier has not provided a new event.

Registered buyers open their own orders. Guests verify access through the email flow on page 14. Public carrier tracking links may show logistics progress; your store must not reveal recipient addresses from an order number alone. Notify only meaningful changes, deduplicate messages and route delivery exceptions to a staff queue.

Uploading a file creates a draft asset; publishing a validated product creates the public page. Provide an optional auto-publish mode only for trusted imports that pass the same checks. The admin should show each step and any failed jobs.
Validate title, primary category, SKU uniqueness, variant price and currency, images, alt text, shipping data and inventory policy. Reject incomplete or unsafe content.
Build a stable slug, default SEO title and description from verified attributes. Preserve staff overrides. Generate useful copy from factual product data; AI suggestions require a factual review.
Commit the catalog changes and product.published or product.updated event in one PostgreSQL transaction. Increment the product version.
Workers refresh catalog search, invalidate product and category caches, regenerate relevant sitemap entries, and schedule Merchant Center feed updates where the store is eligible.
Verify the rendered product HTML, metadata, canonical URL, image URLs and Product offer data. Publish the event version to prevent old retries overwriting newer content.
Brand + product type + important differentiator + store name. Aim for clear concise copy, often around 50 to 60 characters; this is an editorial guide.
One useful sentence explaining the product, verified benefit and delivery or policy detail. Roughly 140 to 160 characters is a drafting guide, not a ranking rule.
Use current variant price and stock policy in visible page content and structured data. Never accept a stale price during checkout.
One intended canonical URL per indexable page. List only canonical, public, successful pages; update lastmod after meaningful changes.
Generate Open Graph title, description and an original share image; keep share assets stable and publicly accessible.

Suggested internal targets: price and stock updates visible in the store within 10 seconds; descriptive content within 60 seconds. For critical catalog changes, expire cached data immediately through an authenticated Next.js handler; ordinary content may use stale-while-revalidate. Test the exact semantics of the pinned Next.js release. [4, 5]
Provide an admin retry queue and alert when publication jobs exceed the target. Search engines choose when to crawl and index; a successful store update does not mean immediate Google ranking.
20 SEO strategy for an expanding catalog

Prioritize a narrow category you can serve well, then expand from search and sales evidence. Automatic metadata supports a scalable catalog, but useful product information, availability, competitive offers and customer trust determine whether visitors buy.
Link home to categories, subcategories and all products using real anchors. Provide paginated URLs as well as any load-more interface. [6]
Fetch representative pages without client execution; crawl the category-to-product path.
Render Product, Offer and BreadcrumbList in HTML. Add valid GTIN or brand where available; match price and availability to visible content. [7]
Rich Results Test plus feed and page consistency checks.
Give selectable variants stable URLs and appropriate ProductGroup relationships. Choose one supported canonical model and use it consistently. [12]
Test color and size deep links, canonical tags and variant offers.
Index curated valuable collections. Control arbitrary sorting and filter combinations; avoid infinite URL spaces. [11]
Crawl budget review; noindex pages must remain crawlable until exclusion is seen.
Write original specifications, sizing, compatibility, comparisons and buying guides based on actual products. Avoid mass thin pages or invented claims. [13]
Editorial review and query-level engagement and sales.
Optimize hero images, responsive formats, font loading, JS weight and layout stability. Target LCP <= 2.5 s, INP <= 200 ms, CLS <= 0.1 at the 75th percentile. [14]
Real-user Core Web Vitals; lab tests before traffic exists.
Keep temporary out-of-stock pages useful. Use a 301 for a genuine replacement, otherwise an honest 404 or 410 when permanently removed.
No redirect chains, soft 404s or archived items in sitemap.

Keep account, checkout, cart, order tracking, internal search and admin pages out of the index. Authentication protects private data; robots.txt does not. Use noindex for suitable crawlable pages and never expect a blocked crawler to read a noindex tag. Apply robots rules to prevent unnecessary facet crawling after assessing existing indexed URLs.

Verify Search Console, submit sitemaps, monitor indexing and structured-data issues, and use Merchant Center free listings where country and product eligibility permit. Do not fabricate reviews, fake stock or keyword-stuff titles. SEO success is measured over time, with no guaranteed position. [7, 13]

There is no method that produces customers with 100% certainty. Use small experiments with margin-based spending limits, then scale the combinations of products, audiences and offers that produce profitable orders.
The first ninety days after launch
Launch 20 to 50 well-documented products in one category. Check mobile checkout, delivery coverage, support and real product photography.
Find usability failures; measure checkout completion and payment success.
Publish useful category guides and comparisons; test one acquisition channel and two offers. Use authentic product demonstrations.
Qualified visits, add-to-cart rate, paid orders and contribution margin by channel.
Improve high-impression low-click pages, simplify checkout and expand proven categories. Collect genuine reviews after delivery.
Organic click-through, conversion, returns and cost per new customer.
Scale profitable campaigns, negotiate fulfillment costs, improve product bundles and introduce a relevant replenishment or loyalty offer.
Repeat purchase, cohort margin, refund rate and inventory turnover.
Show the full payable total and delivery estimate before payment. State returns and warranty clearly. Let buyers check out as guests.
Keep photos and descriptions accurate. Show true availability, useful variants and relevant product comparisons. Avoid fake countdowns or unsupported discount claims.
Make local shipping coverage, support hours and contact methods visible. Use bundles and free-shipping thresholds only when the margin supports them.
Use consented email offers, back-in-stock requests, review requests and repeat-customer rewards. Match each offer to stock and customer interest.

Conversion rate = completed paid orders divided by eligible sessions; report confirmed COD orders separately. CAC = acquisition spend divided by new customers acquired. Contribution per order = net revenue less product cost, payment fees, delivery subsidy, expected returns and variable fulfillment cost.

Example only: if a PKR 5,000 order leaves PKR 1,000 before advertising, PKR 1,000 is an upper break-even acquisition cost before fixed costs. A lower target leaves room for profit. Do not justify high spending with assumed lifetime value before repeat-purchase evidence exists. Compare experiments over sufficient samples; record attribution uncertainty.

Cookies can recognize a browser and remember permitted activity; they cannot reveal an anonymous visitor’s email address. Collect email directly through checkout, account creation or a voluntary subscription. Explain each purpose and use a consent-first marketing design for international reach.
Session, cart, checkout security and fraud controls needed to provide the requested service.
Explain in the cookie notice; keep shopping available without optional tracking.
Pseudonymous page, product, cart and conversion events after the selected consent policy allows them.
Off by default in this recommended baseline; accept or reject with comparable prominence.
Ad pixels, audience exports and behavioral targeting only after the appropriate permission.
Separate optional choice; honor withdrawal and applicable opt-out signals.
Address supplied by the person plus a separate unchecked marketing choice.
Record source, purpose, notice version and time; easy unsubscribe in every promotional email.
Receipts, password recovery, shipment and return notices for the requested transaction.
Keep the content operational; do not add promotional blocks to bypass marketing preferences.

A new visitor may receive a random analytics ID only when permitted. If the visitor later signs in or submits their email, associate only the activity allowed by the disclosed purposes and current permissions. Do not attach past rejected tracking, infer identity from IP addresses, buy anonymous-email matches or use fingerprinting to evade refusal.
Build a preference panel with essential, analytics and advertising purposes. Store the current choice and append grant or withdrawal events. Block optional tags before consent.
Validate consent server-side before marketing jobs, not just in the browser. An analytics choice is not an email subscription. A purchase email is not automatic permission for deals.

Offer access, correction and deletion requests. Set retention periods, for example 90 days for raw behavioral events as a starting product policy, and document separate order-record retention requirements.
Keep emails and addresses out of analytics payloads and URLs. Restrict staff exports, redact logs and review third-party processor settings.

UK ICO guidance distinguishes essential cookies from optional tracking and sets specific electronic-marketing requirements. This blueprint chooses a stricter consent-first default; applicable obligations still depend on customer location and the way the store operates. Review target markets before launch. [15, 16]
Single-use expiring link; strict resend limits; no promotional content.
Order recorded or verified payment event.
Send once per event; distinguish pending, captured and failed payment accurately.
Deduplicate; include secure order access and support details.
Subscription confirmed, preferably through double opt-in.
Marketing permission active; coupon valid; stop when unsubscribed.
Example: 2 hours then 24 hours after inactivity.
Known email plus appropriate marketing permission; cart still exists; stop on purchase or withdrawal.
Use the requested notification permission; do not enroll in unrelated campaigns.
Respect applicable messaging rules; suppress unresolved returns or complaints; no fake review incentives.
Example: opted-in segment or 45 days after purchase.
Current permission, in-stock products and frequency cap; suppress low-engagement recipients.

Commerce events enter the outbox, then a worker evaluates the current customer, order and consent state. Save a deduplication key such as orderId plus eventType. Retry transient errors with exponential backoff, and route exhausted jobs to a visible failure queue. Recheck suppression immediately before sending because permission may change while a job waits.

Maintain campaign templates, preview data, a test-send flow and an approval action. Include sender identity, contact information and a working unsubscribe path in promotional messages. Use a global cap such as two promotional messages per week initially, with separate limits for each automation. Treat all timings here as starting hypotheses to test.

Use a transactional email provider with verified sending domains. Configure SPF, DKIM and DMARC; separate transactional and promotional streams; process bounce, complaint and unsubscribe webhooks; and warm sending gradually. Provide one-click unsubscribe headers for marketing from the start. Gmail imposes additional requirements on bulk senders. [21]

Measure clicks, purchases, unsubscribes and complaints. Open rates are unreliable because privacy features can prefetch images. Prefer campaign revenue and conversion with attribution limits. Store no bought email lists, and do not send deals to visitors who never provided an address and marketing permission.
24 Development phases from discovery to checkout

Planning estimate: 16 to 20 calendar weeks for two experienced full-time developers, with design and QA support, a limited initial catalog, one payment provider and one courier. A solo build can take materially longer. Provider approval and operational readiness can extend the calendar independently of coding.
Confirm merchant model, countries, currency, catalog, variants, fulfillment, return policy and product restrictions. Start payment onboarding. Define requirements and permission matrix.
Scope approved; gateway eligibility evidence requested; one measurable launch goal and prioritized backlog.
Wireframe home, listings, product, cart, guest checkout, account, tracking and admin. Build design tokens, reusable components and mobile prototypes.
Critical flows reviewed at mobile and desktop sizes; keyboard and error states designed.
Create monorepo, CI, staging, migrations, authentication, roles, owner MFA, audit logging, storage and API contracts.
Session, permission and recovery tests pass; clean migration works; staging secrets isolated.
Complete products, categories, variants, imports, stock, search, wishlist and cart. Build quote and guest checkout, reservations, order snapshots and admin order processing.
Staff publish an item; it appears in the correct category; guest and account test orders have correct totals and stock.

For each feature, specify UI states, API contract, schema migration, authorization, domain service, background events and acceptance tests before calling it done. A screen that uses mock data does not satisfy an exit gate. Seed realistic products, a low-stock variant, an unpaid order, a partial refund and a delivery exception for review.
Decisions the owner needs to settle

Confirm store name and branding, target countries, product category, sourcing and stock process, supported currency, warehouse address, delivery partners, return terms and payment entity. Keep these in configuration or documented policy where appropriate; do not bury business choices in controllers.

The schedule assumes a single merchant. Opening the platform to independent sellers changes onboarding, authorization, commissions, settlement, dispute handling and reporting, and requires its own scope and delivery estimate.
25 Development phases from payments to launch
Integrate one approved gateway and courier. Build webhook deduplication, reconciliation, refunds, labels, tracking, partial fulfillment and returns.
Verified payment and shipment complete end to end; decline, timeout, duplicate and refund cases pass.
Complete server-rendered catalog, metadata, JSON-LD, canonical rules, sitemap, redirects and feeds. Add consent controls, email automations and admin retry screens.
Published product updates without redeploy; optional tags stay blocked after rejection; unsubscribe prevents queued marketing.
Performance, accessibility, security, concurrency and recovery tests. Owner acceptance, staff training, fulfillment rehearsal and a limited live pilot.
No unresolved critical defects; restore tested; pilot orders reconciled; launch checklist signed off.
Release gradually, monitor payment and job health, run acquisition experiments, fix real customer friction and tune inventory operations.
Stable checkout and fulfillment; daily reconciliation; prioritized improvements based on real usage.

Product owner supplies product information, pricing, policies and merchant applications. Frontend engineer owns storefront and admin interactions. Backend engineer owns data integrity, integrations and security rules. Designer validates usability and consistency. QA verifies business flows, privacy choices and failure cases. One person can hold multiple roles, but each gate still needs an owner.
Payment provider approval, eligible products, settlement account, verified domain and access to live credentials.
Courier account, delivery coverage, COD process if offered, packaging and a person responsible for dispatch and returns.
Accurate product images, weights, dimensions, opening stock, tax configuration and legally appropriate customer policies.
Production backups, alert recipients, customer support contact, email domain authentication and successful live pilot refunds.

The owner can add and publish stock, a guest can pay and track delivery, a customer can manage their account, staff can fulfill and refund, and the business can reconcile money. The system remains usable when optional tracking is rejected. Release gates measure these outcomes rather than counting pages or components.

Prioritize tests that protect money, access, stock and customer communications. Use unit tests for pricing and state rules, integration tests against PostgreSQL for transactions, provider sandbox tests, and Playwright for critical browser journeys.
Register, verify, login and logout work; revoked session cannot access private data.
Guest places order without registration; access requires verification; account claim links only verified orders.
Catalog staff cannot refund or change roles; direct API calls are rejected and logged.
Product, images, category, title, description, price, stock and JSON-LD become consistent without a deployment.
Two concurrent orders for one unit cannot create two valid reservations or negative stock.
Forged, wrong-amount and wrong-currency events cannot mark paid; valid duplicates have one effect.
A lost response or webhook resolves to the original attempt, without a duplicate charge or abandoned captured order.
Partial refund cannot exceed captured balance; partial shipping cannot exceed purchased quantity; return disposition controls restock.
Reject optional cookies: no optional tags fire. Withdraw email permission: queued offers stop; operational notices still work.
Useful HTML and canonical links exist; structured data validates; checkout supports keyboard and readable error states.
Worker restart, duplicate event and provider outage preserve order correctness and expose an actionable retry queue.
Backup restore succeeds; logs redact secrets; alerting works; reconciliation balances the live pilot orders.

Load-test realistic catalog filters and checkout concurrency. Start with a documented target such as 50 concurrent checkout attempts with no integrity errors; increase to the forecast launch load. Set internal API latency and error budgets from staging measurements, excluding the external provider delay rather than hiding it from customer timings.

Measure Core Web Vitals on mobile, not only a desktop Lighthouse score. Keep a rollback procedure ready, use backward-compatible migrations, and prevent fulfillment of unverified payments during the pilot. [14]

Host the Next.js application on a suitable managed platform or Node runtime, and deploy NestJS and workers as long-running processes with health checks. Use managed PostgreSQL, Redis, object storage and a CDN. Ensure a shared catalog-cache strategy if Next.js runs on multiple instances. Keep application regions close to the database.
Lint, type check, test, dependency review, build, migration dry run, staging acceptance, then controlled production deployment.
Connection pooling, least-privilege users, slow-query monitoring, daily backups and point-in-time recovery where available.
Retry policy, dead-letter queue, idempotent consumers and alerts for lag. Reconcile unfinished work from PostgreSQL, not Redis alone.
Daily compare orders, attempts, refunds, provider statements and settlement bank records. Investigate mismatches and aged processing states.
Track checkout failures, webhook errors, stock conflicts, publication lag, email bounces, courier sync age and unusual admin actions.
Named owner, support contact, disable affected gateway if necessary, retain evidence, communicate order impact and document recovery.
Initial business targets: RPO 15 minutes and RTO 4 hours if funded and technically supported; prove with a restore exercise.
Use pagination and selective indexes; measure search relevance and query latency before adding a dedicated search cluster.

Request separate quotes for engineering, design and QA; cloud application hosting; database and Redis; storage and image delivery; transactional and promotional email; observability; payment processing and FX; courier and returns; security review; and ongoing maintenance. Costs depend on order volume, geography, catalog and provider contracts, so do not treat a hosting quote as the whole operating budget.

Daily: payment reconciliation, dispatch exceptions, stock alerts and failed jobs. Weekly: query and sales performance, email complaints, returns and admin audit review. Monthly: dependency maintenance, restore drill or documented recovery check, access review, customer feedback and experiment results.
Launch with the smallest dependable configuration and reserve maintenance time. Advanced recommendations, loyalty points and a native app should follow evidence of demand, not delay a working store.
